title: ML Infrastructure Engineer - New Grad

description_preview:
SambaNova is a leader in next-generation AI infrastructure, delivering a full-stack inference platform for customers worldwide. At the core of SambaNova's technology is the RDU (Reconfigurable Dataflow Unit) — a chip built on a dataflow architecture rather than the traditional GPU model. Its decode performance is especially strong for agentic workloads like multi-turn agents, code generation, and long-running applications. RDUs are packaged into SambaRack, rack-scale hardware that lets customers deploy state-of-the-art models with better performance, greater energy efficiency, and faster time to value.
About The Team
The ML Infrastructure team builds and operates the inference stack that serves SambaNova's models on our RDU accelerators. We cover request scheduling, caching, decoding techniques, public APIs, and the accuracy testing that every inference feature must pass before it ships.
About The Role
As a new grad ML Infrastructure Engineer, you'll write production Python for our inference serving stack, including our vLLM integration and public APIs. You'll help bring features like speculative decoding, prompt caching, and tool calling into production on the RDU, and add accuracy and regression tests that catch problems before customers do.
Responsibilities
Implement inference features on the RDU such as speculative decoding, constrained decoding, tool calling, prompt caching, and long-context inference
Adapt vLLM and related serving frameworks to the RDU architecture
Build and maintain endpoints in the public inference API
Write accuracy verification and regression tests for inference features
Debug latency, throughput, and reliability issues in production services
Required Qualifications
B.S. in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or related field
Strong programming skills in Python
Understanding of algorithms, data structures, concurrency, and systems design
Coursework or project experience in distributed systems or machine learning
Experience with LLM serving frameworks such as vLLM, SGLang, or TensorRT-LLM
Experience with inference techniques such as speculative decoding, KV caching, or continuous batching
Experience with PyTorch
Preferred Qualifications
M.S. or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or related field
Experience building or maintaining APIs or backend services
Internship or research experience in ML systems or backend infrastructure
Experience with disaggregated systems - prefill/decode
Open source project ownership or contributions
Base Salary Range:
Base Pay Range
$131,200—$196,800 USD
Submission Guidelines
Please note that in order to be considered an applicant for any position at SambaNova Systems, you must submit an application form for each position for which you believe you are qualified.
EEO Policy
SambaNova Systems is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard basis of age (40 and over), color, disability, gender identity, genetic information, marital status, military or veteran status, national origin/ancestry, race, religion, creed, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding), sexual orientation, and any other applicable status protected by federal, state, or local laws.
Benefits Summary For US-Based, Full-Time Employment Positions
SambaNova offers a competitive total rewards package, including the base salary, plus equity and benefits. We cover 95% premium coverage for employee medical insurance, and 77% premium coverage for dependents and offer a Health Savings Account (HSA) with employer contribution. We also offer Dental, Vision, Short/Long term Disability, Basic Life, Voluntary Life, and AD&D insurance plans in addition to Flexible Spending Account (FSA) options like Health Care, Limited Purpose, and Dependent Care. Our library of well-being benefits available to you and your dependents includes a full subscription to Headspace, Gympass+ membership with access to physical gyms, One Medical membership, counseling services with an Employee Assistance Program, and much more.

Job Description
Your Work Shapes the World at Caterpillar Inc.
When you join Caterpillar, you're joining a global team who cares not just about the work we do – but also about each other. We are the makers, problem solvers, and future world builders who are creating stronger, more sustainable communities. We don't just talk about progress and innovation here – we make it happen, with our customers, where we work and live. Together, we are building a better world, so we can all enjoy living in it.
As an AI Engineer, you will design, develop, and optimize advanced AI interactions to power production-grade software applications. You will move beyond basic prompt drafting to build robust, scalable, and reliable AI systems utilizing state-of-the-art Large Language Models (LLMs). Your role is critical in orchestrating autonomous AI agents, implementing
Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
pipelines, and establishing
rigorous testing and observability frameworks
. You will bridge the gap between complex business logic and machine intelligence, ensuring high-quality, safe, and deterministic AI behaviors.
What You Will Do
Prompt Architecture & Tuning
Design Advanced Prompts: Architect, version, and refine highly effective system, contextual, and dynamic prompts using advanced techniques (e.g., Chain-of-Thought, Tree-of-Thoughts, ReAct, Few-Shot learning).
Mitigate Risks: Minimize model hallucinations, jailbreaking, and prompt injections through programmatic guardrails and robust adversarial prompting strategies.
Model Agnostic Tuning: Adapt, benchmark, and fine-tune prompt structures across diverse open-source and proprietary frontier models.
Agentic Workflows & RAG Systems
Build AI Agents: Design and orchestrate multi-agent systems and multi-step reasoning workflows using frameworks like LangGraph, LangChain.
Optimize RAG Pipelines: Integrate and fine-tune Retrieval-Augmented Generation architectures, managing semantic search, chunking strategies, embedding models, and vector database queries.
Tool Execution: Implement precise function-calling and tool-use prompts enabling LLMs to interact reliably with external APIs, databases, and legacy codebases.
Testing, Evaluation & Observability
Build automated testing suites using RAGAS and Evals frameworks to assess RAG accuracy and enable continuous validation and benchmarking of Retrieval‑Augmented Generation outputs across datasets and Models .
Agent Testing: Build automated regression testing suites and CI/CD pipelines to validate prompt stability, agent trajectory correctness, and tool-calling accuracy.
Implement LLM Observability: Set up production monitoring and observability systems using platforms like Azure Application insights, Microsoft Foundry.
Monitor Metrics: Track, analyze, and optimize production runtime metrics including semantic drift, token usage, cost efficiencies, and end-to-end latency.
Collaboration & Continuous Innovation
Cross-Functional Delivery: Work alongside Product Managers, Data Scientists, and Software Engineers to translate commercial requirements into deterministic AI capabilities.
Technology Scouting: Keep pace with rapid weekly advancements in LLM capabilities, evaluation frameworks, and orchestration libraries to sustain a competitive edge.
What You Have
Core Prompt Engineering: Expert-level mastery of structured prompt formats (XML, JSON wrappers), system-level steering, and context-window optimization.
Production Programming: High proficiency in Python or TypeScript for constructing backend AI logic, processing asynchronous data streams, and handling API integrations.
Orchestration Frameworks: Hands-on experience building apps using LangChain, LangGraph, native SDKs.
Vector Infrastructure: Solid experience working with vector databases (e.g., Azure AI Search, AWS Open Search) and hybrid search retrieval methods.
Data & ML Fundamentals: Strong capabilities in data manipulation (Pandas, NumPy), data cleaning, token handling, and foundational understanding of NLP transformers.

reason: Stack +34; Title fit +6; New Grad +20; US +10
description_preview:
SambaNova is a leader in next-generation AI infrastructure, delivering a full-stack inference platform for customers worldwide. At the core of SambaNova's technology is the RDU (Reconfigurable Dataflow Unit) — a chip built on a dataflow architecture rather than the traditional GPU model. Its decode performance is especially strong for agentic workloads like multi-turn agents, code generation, and long-running applications. RDUs are packaged into SambaRack, rack-scale hardware that lets customers deploy state-of-the-art models with better performance, greater energy efficiency, and faster time to value.
About The Team
The Runtime team owns the lowest level of the SambaNova software stack, the layer that talks directly to the hardware. We build the user libraries, drivers, networking, and system tools that run ML training and inference across SambaStack and SambaCloud.
About The Role
As a new grad Runtime Engineer, you'll write production code in C/C++/Rust and Python across drivers, user space libraries, networking, and system tools. You'll help bring up drivers on next generation silicon, test and deploy runtime features on large multi-node systems, and track down performance bottlenecks with the hardware and compiler teams.
Responsibilities
Develop and maintain kernel drivers for next generation SambaNova silicon
Build user space libraries that make efficient use of hardware resources
Find and fix networking bottlenecks within and across nodes
Build tools for profiling, debugging, and job and hardware management
Test and deploy runtime features on large multi-node systems
Work with the hardware and compiler teams to diagnose and fix performance issues
Required Qualifications
B.S. in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or related field
Strong programming skills in C/C++/Rust and Python
Experience with high speed networking such as RDMA, RoCE, or InfiniBand
Experience with distributed communication libraries such as MPI, NCCL, or UCX
Experience writing Linux kernel drivers or other system level software
Experience with Linux and debugging tools such as GDB
Preferred Qualifications
M.S. or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or related field
Familiarity with PCIe
Experience with profiling or performance analysis tools
Internship or research experience in systems software, networking, or performance engineering
Open source project ownership or contributions

$131,200—$196,200 USD

Job Summary
IPAC at Caltech has an opening for an Associate Applications Developer to participate in the development of the data processing pipelines for the UVEX mission.
IPAC, part of the Physics, Math, and Astronomy Division at Caltech (www.caltech.edu), provides science operations, user support, data and archive services, and scientific vision to maximize discovery with observatories both in space and on the ground.

title: Software Engineer - Manipulation
reason: Stack +40; Synergy +10; Title fit +12; Exp fit +6; US +10; Senior salary -45
description_preview:
Apptronik is a human-centered robotics company developing AI-powered robots to support humanity in every facet of life. Our flagship humanoid robot, Apollo, is built to collaborate thoughtfully with people, starting with critical industries such as manufacturing and logistics, with future applications in healthcare, the home, and beyond.
We operate at the cutting edge of Applied AI, applying our expertise across the full robotics stack to solve some of society's most important problems. You will join a team dedicated to bringing Apollo to market at scale, tackling the complex challenges like safety, commercialization, and mass production to change the world for the better.
JOB SUMMARY
The Software Engineer - Manipulation is a core contributor to our robot's ability to interact with the world reliably and precisely. This role is responsible for developing and deploying learning-based manipulation policies, with a focus on post-training methods that adapt and improve those policies on real tasks and physical hardware.
This role will bridge the gap between cutting-edge research and scalable, reliable production software. Working closely with the simulation, data, hardware, and systems teams, this engineer will take manipulation policies from demonstration data through post-training to robust deployment across our fleet.
ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES or KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES
Implement and deploy state-of-the-art learning-based manipulation policies to achieve reliable, world-class performance on real-world tasks with physical hardware.
Adapt and improve policies for new tasks and hardware using post-training methods such as RL fine-tuning, policy distillation, and interactive imitation learning (e.g., DAgger).
Build and maintain the data pipelines that support post-training, including teleoperation and demonstration collection, retargeting, dataset aggregation, and curation.
Drive the development cycle from simulation and offline evaluation to robustly transferring and fine-tuning policies on the robot.
Develop visuomotor policies for grasping, in-hand manipulation, and whole-arm manipulation, with reliable, low-latency execution on hardware.
Define evaluation metrics and regression tests for policy performance in simulation and on hardware, and use the results to guide technical decisions.
Collaborate closely with the simulation, data, hardware, and systems teams to diagnose system-level issues and co-develop solutions.
Maintain high standards for the codebase through testing, documentation, and peer code reviews.
SKILLS AND REQUIREMENTS
Technical Skills (Must-Have)
Manipulation:
Strong experience in robotic manipulation, including grasping, in-hand or whole-arm control, and high-DOF motion, with a track record of hardware deployment.
Learning-Based Control:
Hands-on experience training and debugging learned policies, including post-training methods such as RL fine-tuning, distillation, and imitation learning (e.g., DAgger).
Software Engineering:
Proficiency in Python, C++, and PyTorch or JAX, with experience building real-time robotic software stacks.
Data & Evaluation:
Experience working with demonstration and teleoperation data, and building evaluation pipelines for learned policies.
Good to Have
Simulation Environments:
Experience with physics engines such as IsaacSim, MuJoCo, or Drake for policy training and validation.
Generalist Policies:
Experience adapting large, general-purpose manipulation policies to specific tasks and embodiments.
Teleoperation:
Experience with VR/haptic interfaces and retargeting algorithms for human-in-the-loop control.
Tactile Sensing:
Experience integrating tactile/haptic feedback into manipulation pipelines.
Computer Vision:
Familiarity with 6D pose estimation, point cloud processing, or visual-servoing.
EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE
An MS with 3+ years of relevant experience, or a recent PhD, in Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field.
Relevant experience specifically focused on learning-based manipulation or a closely related area.
A proven track record of taking learned policies from a research/simulation environment and successfully deploying them on physical hardware.
PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS
Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer
Must be able to lift 15 pounds at times
Vision to read printed materials and a computer screen
Hearing and speech to communicate
The annual salary range is $180,000 - $240,000
This is a direct hire. Please, no outside Agency solicitations.

At PNNL, our core capabilities are divided among major departments that we refer to as Directorates within the Lab, focused on a specific area of scientific research or other function, with its own leadership team and dedicated budget.
Our Science & Technology directorates include National Security, Integrated Discovery Sciences, and Energy and Environment. In addition, we have an Environmental Molecular Sciences Laboratory, a Department of Energy, Office of Science user facility housed on the PNNL campus.
The Integrated Discovery Sciences Directorate (IDSD) leads fundamental research across biology, chemistry, earth and environmental sciences, materials science, advanced computing, artificial intelligence, quantum information science, mathematics, autonomy, and DOE national user facilities. Who We Are
Nuro believes self-driving vehicles are the most immediate and profound opportunity for AI to drive positive change in the physical world. Safer streets, more time for what matters, and easier access to the world around us, that’s why we’re building a universal autonomy platform: self-driving for all roads and all rides.
Founded in 2016, Nuro is a physical AI company developing Level 4 autonomous driving technology for a wide range of vehicles, use cases, and markets. Powered by the Nuro Driver™, our universal autonomy platform enables the global mobility ecosystem to deploy autonomy at scale, from robotaxis and logistics fleets to personal vehicles.
With years of real-world deployment experience and a flexible, partner-led business model, Nuro is working toward a future where millions of autonomous vehicles powered by our technology help make everyday life safer, easier, and more connected.
Nuro has raised over $2B in capital from Uber, NVIDIA, Google, Softbank, Fidelity, T. Rowe Price, and other leading investors.
About The Role
Nuro operates real self-driving vehicles on public roads today — not a research platform, not ADAS. The Embedded Software Engineering team builds the software for the safety-critical embedded controllers that connect the Nuro Driver™ to the vehicle: the devices that command steering, braking, and propulsion, alongside other vehicle actuators, distribute and monitor power, monitor vehicle motion, and bring the vehicle to a safe state when something goes wrong.
As an Embedded Software Engineer, you will work across the full stack of multicore automotive microcontrollers from RTOS, drivers, and scheduler up through middleware and application components that talk to the vehicle, and help extend that stack as our hardware evolves. You will bring the Nuro Driver™ up on new vehicle platforms alongside OEM and supplier engineers, and see your code drive real vehicles on public roads. We're hiring across levels, from engineers with a couple years of embedded experience to those who've shipped a production automotive launch.
About The Work
Design, implement and test embedded C software for safety-critical multicore automotive microcontrollers, spanning base software such as RTOS, device drivers, scheduling and bootloader, middleware such as inter-component messaging and end-to-end protection, and application components such as actuator interface, body controls, power management and fault management.
Integrate the Nuro Driver™ with new vehicle platforms: define and implement CAN and Ethernet interfaces with OEM ECUs, adapt actuator and body-control interfaces, and validate them on bench and in vehicle.
Take part in hands-on device and vehicle bring-up, prototyping and debugging on multiple vehicle platforms, from first power-on to autonomous driving.
Build and maintain the team's verification infrastructure: unit tests, hardware-in-the-loop benches and vehicle test procedures.
Work within an ISO 26262 development process: define software requirements from system safety requirements, then implement and verify them with full traceability.
Collaborate daily with systems, safety, hardware, controls and autonomy engineers, and with OEM and supplier partners, from definition through verification.
About You
B.S. or higher in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering or a closely related field.
2+ years of industry experience developing embedded software in C, including work on a real-time operating system.
Solid computer science fundamentals: data structures, concurrency and algorithm design.
Working knowledge of microcontroller internals and peripherals, with depth in at least one of device driver development, CAN or automotive Ethernet, bootloaders and software update, embedded security, or vehicle-level integration and test.
Strong problem-solving and debugging skills, clear written and spoken communication, and a track record of working well with engineers from other disciplines.
Comfortable at the bench with debug probes, oscilloscopes, logic analyzers and CAN tools. You enjoy finding out why hardware and software disagree.
Bonus Points
3+ years of embedded development in the automotive or autonomous vehicle industry, including a production launch.
Hands-on functional safety experience with ISO 26262, or safety-critical development in another regulated industry such as DO-178C or IEC 62304.
Experience with Infineon AURIX TC3xx, SafeRTOS or FreeRTOS, or AUTOSAR Classic base software such as MCAL and communication stacks.
Vehicle network integration experience: DBC and ARXML, UDS diagnostics, E2E protection, time synchronization.
Knowledge of vehicle functions, vehicle dynamics or control theory.

description_preview:
You build working customer solutions, not isolated features that may never reach a user. You like the hard middle: vague requirements, messy APIs, structured content, authentication flows, migration scripts, and the moment a customer can finally run their workflow end to end. If you want neatly scoped tickets with little customer contact, this is not the right fit.
Quark helps enterprise teams manage complex content workflows. In this role, you will turn customer needs into reliable implementations on the Quark platform: configurations, REST API integrations, webhooks, SSO/SAML connections, XML/XSLT transforms, migrations, and workflow automations. The work is technical, customer-facing, and outcome-based. A good demo is not enough. The solution must work in real conditions, be tested against acceptance criteria, and be clear enough for others to support.
AI is part of how the work gets done. You will use tools such as Claude Code or Cursor to move faster, and you will build practical AI agents, Skill files, or similar automation assets that reduce repeat work. Over time, your impact grows from delivering single implementations to creating reusable delivery patterns that make future customer rollouts faster and more reliable.
If you want hands-on integration work where AI, structured content, and customer value meet, apply now.
What You Will Be Doing
Turn customer requirements into technical implementation plans, acceptance criteria, and delivery tasks
Configure Quark workflows, structured content models, rules, integrations, and external data-source connections
Build and test REST API, webhook, SSO/SAML, XML/XSLT, migration, and scripting-based automation deliverables
Diagnose implementation defects by analyzing logs, payloads, authentication flows, transforms, and configuration dependencies
Create concise runbooks, handover materials, and walkthroughs that help customers operate the delivered solution
What You Won’t Be Doing
Building unrelated core product features with no direct customer implementation goal
Working from vague tickets without clarifying requirements, constraints, and acceptance criteria
Applying temporary workarounds without root-cause analysis, validation, and reusable documentation
Handing off generic training decks that leave customers dependent on undocumented tribal knowledge
Waiting weeks to perfect a solution before showing tested working progress
Implementation Engineer Key Responsibilities
Deliver reliable Quark customer implementations that connect systems, content workflows, and users to measurable customer value.
Basic Requirements
At least 3 years of hands-on software engineering, systems integration, implementation, or technical consulting experience
Experience building or troubleshooting REST API and webhook integrations
Working knowledge of authentication concepts such as SSO or SAML
Practical proficiency with XML and XSLT or an equivalent structured-data transformation technology
Proficiency in at least one scripting or programming language used for migration, automation, or workflow implementation
Regular practical use of AI developer tools such as Claude Code or Cursor
Experience building at least one useful AI agent, Skill file, agent definition, or equivalent automation artifact
Fluent in written and spoken English for customer discovery, requirements clarification, and technical handover
Availability for at least 4 hours per day overlapping with business hours for US customers and 4 hours for Europe.
Nice-to-have Requirements
Experience with content management, publishing platforms, or structured content workflows
Experience creating customer-facing technical documentation, runbooks, or implementation handover materials
Experience converting ambiguous customer requirements into end-to-end integrations, migrations, or workflow automations

We’re talking software engineers, AI specialists, product leaders, marketers, analysts, and operators - tech people who excel in autonomous, high-performance, remote-first environments.

associate Systems Engineer

Sapphire for BDS is Boeing’s enterprise modernization program to standardize and unify digital engineering, supply chain, and manufacturing processes across defense platforms. Salesforce Platform Engineer, Mid
The Opportunity:
At the intersection of technical expertise and platform engineering lies the role of a Salesforce Platform Engineer. When you've built and supported Salesforce solutions and can contribute to development, integration, automation, and platform improvements while ensuring quality, scalability, and maintainability, you are ready to grow with our team.
As a Salesforce Platform Engineer on our team, you'll spend most of your time protecting release quality, including designing test strategy, validating platform changes, and catching issues before they reach production, while also contributing hands-on to configuration and development work. This is a role for QA-minded engineers who want a real seat at the build table, not just a downstream gate. You'll work closely with a build-focused counterpart on the team, and over time you'll build the range to step into either seat as the team needs. Due to the nature of work performed within this facility, U.S. citizenship is required.

Experience with Salesforce DevOps tools and practices, including GitHub or Salesforce DX
Knowledge of Apex and Lightning Web Components to read, debug, and validate code changes

description_preview:
If you want to be part of a dynamic team delivering cutting-edge cyber training solutions, this is the place for you. Amentum is seeking a Software Engineer to join the DevOps team in Hanover, MD. The team develops, deploys, and supports mission-focused cyber training solutions used across multiple locations.
Team members work in a collaborative, multidisciplinary environment supporting the entire software development lifecycle, including requirements analysis, software development, testing, deployment, infrastructure management, and operational support. Engineers work closely with instructors, developers, and system administrators to deliver reliable, realistic training capabilities.
Unlike many software organizations where engineers are assigned to a single product or technology stack, members of the DevOps team contribute across a diverse portfolio of applications, services, and supporting infrastructure. This provides opportunities to build broad technical expertise while collaborating with teammates to deliver integrated solutions throughout the software development lifecycle.
This position is ideal for software engineers who enjoy solving complex technical challenges, learning new technologies, and applying their skills across a diverse portfolio of software, infrastructure, and operational systems.
Work Schedule:
The courses being supported are active from 0700-1800 M-F. Contract core hours are 1000-1400. The DevOps team is flexible on arrival and departure time however there are occasions where one or more DevOps team members will be needed to support testing and maintenance before or after course hours.
Essential Responsibilities:
The Software Engineer will contribute to the design, development, deployment, and maintenance of software applications and supporting infrastructure. Team members are expected to broaden their experience across multiple areas of the software development lifecycle while developing technical expertise in one or more areas.
Responsibilities include:
Design, develop, troubleshoot, and maintain software applications supporting cyber training environments.
Analyze requirements and develop technical solutions that support mission and customer needs.
Develop user interfaces, backend services, APIs, automation tools, and data processing solutions.
Contribute to the implementation and maintenance of software development pipelines.
Configure, deploy, and maintain applications in virtualized and containerized environments.
Develop and maintain databases, dataflows, scripts, and automation solutions.
Support the creation and maintenance of realistic cyber training environments and simulations.
Perform software testing, debugging, validation, and analysis of results.
Evaluate new technologies and contribute recommendations for improving applications and development processes.
Document software designs, configurations, processes, and operational procedures.
Collaborate with instructors, developers, system administrators, and other technical teams to improve training capabilities.
Identify opportunities to improve existing applications, workflows, and user experiences.
Security Clearance Required:
TS/SCI with Poly
Minimum Education& Years of Experience:
Master's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Systems, or related field and two (2) years of relevant experience;
OR
Bachelor's degree in the same fields and five (5) years of relevant experience;
OR Associate's degree (or 18 semester hours of military coursework/training in a computer-related field) and seven (7) years of relevant experience;
OR High school diploma/GED and nine (9) years of relevant experience.
Minimum Requirements (Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities):
LCAT Domain Specialized Requirements
Programming Languages: Proficiency in one or more of the following (or equivalent): Java, Ruby/Rails, Python, C++
Web/UI: Experience with web UI technologies such as HTML, CSS, JavaScript and common patterns (AJAX/fetch, JSON)
Databases: Experience using SQL and relational databases (e.g., MySQL/PostgreSQL or equivalent)
Platforms: Working knowledge of windows and Linux environments
Dev Workflow: Experience with CI build/test pipelines and issue tracking (e.g., JIRA or equivalent)
Preferred Qualifications:
The ideal candidate has experience contributing to software development, DevOps, or application support activities and a desire to expand their knowledge across the software development lifecycle.
Team members may initially bring deeper experience in areas such as user interfaces, backend services, infrastructure, automation, or deployment. These areas represent technical strengths rather than separate roles. Engineers are expected to expand their skills across the full software development and deployment lifecycle.
Role Expectations
Independently develops, deploys, and supports software capabilities.
Owns components or applications while collaborating across technical areas.
Contributes improvements to development processes, automation, and system reliability.
Participates in design discussions.
Troubleshoots production issues.
Can move between projects with minimal ramp-up.
All team members are expected to develop familiarity with the team's full portfolio of applications, products, services, and supporting infrastructure.

Developing modern web applications, backend services, APIs, automation tools, or data processing solutions.

Deploying and supporting applications in Linux and Windows environments using virtualization and container technologies.
Developing scripts, automation, and deployment solutions to improve operational efficiency.
Integrating software with supporting infrastructure, networking, and application services.

Centurion is seeking a Mid-Level DevSecOps Engineer to support and enhance enterprise shared services platforms utilized by development teams across the organization. The successful candidate will help drive CI/CD modernization, cloud-native adoption, security integration, and operational excellence while partnering with development, platform, and security teams to deliver reliable and scalable solutions.
Design, develop, maintain, and optimize CI/CD pipelines using Pipeline as Code, shared libraries, automated testing, and deployment orchestration.
Support migration initiatives from on-premises and self-hosted solutions to SaaS and cloud-native platforms.
Build, maintain, and secure containerized workloads using Docker, Podman, Kubernetes, and OpenShift technologies.
Implement DevSecOps best practices including SAST, SCA, vulnerability scanning, secrets management, RBAC, and secure software delivery processes.
Develop and maintain Infrastructure as Code (IaC) solutions using Terraform, CloudFormation, or similar technologies.
Support AWS cloud environments including IAM, Fargate, ECR, S3, CloudWatch, and related cloud services.
Manage source control processes utilizing Git, branching strategies, pull requests, and automated quality controls.
Develop automation and operational tooling using Python, Java, Node.js, Bash, PowerShell, or other scripting languages.
Configure and maintain artifact repositories and dependency management solutions such as Nexus and Artifactory.
Monitor and support platform health through observability and logging solutions including Prometheus, Grafana, ELK Stack, OpenSearch, and CloudWatch.
Troubleshoot and resolve complex build, deployment, integration, and infrastructure issues across development and production environments.
Collaborate with development, security, and infrastructure teams to improve platform reliability, scalability, and security.
Support vulnerability remediation, compliance initiatives, and continuous improvement efforts across the software delivery lifecycle.
Contribute to documentation, platform standards, operational procedures, and engineering best practices
REQUIRED SKILLS:
Ability to obtain and maintain US Public Trust Clearance
Bachelor’s degree and 3+ years IT related experience
3+ years of experience in DevOps, DevSecOps, Platform Engineering, or related disciplines.
Hands-on experience with CI/CD pipeline development and automation.
Experience with container technologies including Docker, Podman, or CRI-O.
Experience with Kubernetes, OpenShift, or similar orchestration platforms.
Experience working within AWS cloud environments.
Proficiency in at least two programming or scripting languages such as Python, Java, Node.js, Go, .NET/C#, Bash, or PowerShell.
Experience with Infrastructure as Code solutions such as Terraform or CloudFormation.
Knowledge of application security principles, vulnerability management, and DevSecOps practices.
Experience with Git-based source control and collaborative development workflows.
Strong troubleshooting, analytical, and communication skills.
DESIRED SKILLS:
Experience supporting enterprise platform engineering or shared services environments.
Experience integrating security tooling into CI/CD pipelines.
AWS, Kubernetes, Terraform, or security-related certifications.
Experience with Agile software development methodologies.
Familiarity with federal, regulated, or compliance-driven environments.

Job Description
Igniters operate in the world’s most demanding environment. Igniters are self-motivated, mission-driven, and relentless in solving the Warfighters’ hardest problems. We move fast, think differently, and execute with precision to tackle high-stakes challenges across AI/ML, space and missile defense intelligence, EMSO, advanced analytics, and programmatic domains. As an employee-owned SDVOSB headquartered in Huntsville, AL, our team delivers mission-critical impact for the Army, Air Force, Space Force, MDA, NASA, DIA, and FBI.
Ignite exists to outpace the threat and deliver results that matter in the moments that count.
Ignite is currently seeking driven, detail-oriented
Digital Engineers
to support intelligence analysis and modeling efforts for the
National Air and Space Intelligence Center (NASIC)
. The Modeling, Analytics, and Simulation Sciences (MASS) Operation is seeking a Digital Engineer to support our customers at the National Air and Space Intelligence Center (NASIC). As a Digital Engineer on our team, you will use your combined MBSE and software knowledge/experience to help shape and implement digital solutions and services for our customers. You will work alongside engineers and software developers to develop authoritative engineering models that contribute to our nation’s defense. You’ll apply your knowledge of engineering processes, tools, methods, and programs to design and integrate system architectures, interfaces, and workflows to support Department of Defense (DoD) processes. Familiarity with domains such as defense, aerospace, or information technology is highly beneficial.. Positions are expected to be Onsite in Dayton, OH.

Bachelor’s Degree in Systems Engineering, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Aerospace, or related technical field
Minimum of 3 years of relevant experience
Experience using DE and MBSE tools and processes to create and manage tailored model-based artifacts that meet customer requirements
Knowledge of object-oriented programming languages, including Java, C++, or Python
Experience with software engineering and integrating different software platforms/tools
Strong knowledge of SysML/UML for modeling architectures and system behaviors
Proficiency with MBSE methodologies and tools (e.g., Cameo Systems Modeler, MagicDraw, IBM Rhapsody, Enterprise Architect)
Experience with relational Ontologies, APIs, and designing schemas for workflows
Familiarity with DE concepts such as Digital Thread/Digital Twin applications, automation, and integration of MBSE across organizations
Ability to work effectively in a multi-disciplinary team environment, including internal staff, external contractors, and government customers
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to produce and present technical documentation and artifacts
Active TS/SCI security clearance

Bachelor’s Degree in STEM
Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) and SysML Experience
Preferred Qualifications
Master’s Degree in Engineering field or related certifications such as OCSMP Certifications, INCOSE CSEP, or Project Management PMP (among others)
Proven experience leading engineering teams through all phases of the Systems Engineering lifecycle using Digital Engineering methodologies
Knowledge of SysML 2.0
Experience in managing data from interdisciplinary and various program protection levels
Knowledge and interest in interdisciplinary work spanning Systems Engineering, Computer Science, and Data Science
Knowledge of configuration management, risk management, and cybersecurity
Experience with DoD Architecture Framework (DoDAF), Unified Architecture Framework (UAF), or other architecture frameworks.

Today,
Electronic Warfare (EW) is a growing enterprise - protecting the warfighter and our national security against ever-adapting threats

research & development and advanced prototyping, transforming state of the art signal processing algorithms into real-time software systems

Contributing to design and development of advanced systems as a part of multi-disciplinary teams. These teams are made up of other software team members and subject matter experts from the areas of systems engineering, hardware, firmware, machine learning, RF front end design, and signal processing.
Designing, implementing, and testing real-time C/C++ software for multi-core systems running Linux or a real-time operating systems, such as VxWorks
Build software products that utilize third party mathematics and communication libraries
Interface communication standards / protocols such as TCP/IP, UDP, and DDS
Read and understand signal processing algorithms written in MATLAB
Work with Linux operating system as well as experience with real-time operating systems
Designing, implementing, and testing software to configure and control RF hardware devices
Integrating software into third-party software frameworks and architectures, such as Redhawk
Documenting the developed systems
Support system field testing and collection events, usually about a week in duration once or twice a year

Join us and make a difference in Electronic Warfare Technology!

Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or Computer Science, or related discipline

Experience with software testing tools and methodology

Demonstrated ability and motivation to continually learn new technical skills and concepts
Understanding of unit test frameworks and test-driven development practices

Bonus Education/experience
Master’s Degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or equivalent
Active security clearance higher than the Secret level
Ability to debug embedded systems using tools like oscilloscopes and logic analyzers
Experience maintaining, tracking, and updating ticket/status using Gitlab or similar interface
Experience using common scripting languages (e.g. bash)
